thread.title: Judge denies defense bid to dismiss murder charge over undisclosed evidence
thread.title_full: Judge denies defense bid to dismiss murder charge over undisclosed evidence

author: FOX10News
title: Judge denies defense bid to dismiss murder charge over undisclosed evidence
text:
A judge on Thursday denied a murder defendant’s bid to dismiss the case against him based on allegations that key evidence was withheld from the defense.
MOBILE, Ala. - A judge on Thursday denied a murder defendant’s bid to dismiss the case against him based on allegations that key evidence was withheld from the defense.
A judge last month granted a mistrial after determining that prosecutors had failed to turn over a report on a cell phone extraction. A lawyer for the defendant, Mobile resident William Malik Glover, argued at a hearing Thursday that the case should be dismissed entirely.
“The State cannot simply wash its hands of MPD’s refusal to produce certain, relevant and owed discovery,” defense attorney Tom Walsh wrote in a court filing. But Mobile County Circuit Judge Michael Windom disagreed. The Mobile County District Attorney’s Office has said that it missed the report in its pretrial review. Prosecutors allege that Glover fatally shot Al Dimitri Craig on Flicker Drive in 2023.
Walsh noted that before he took the case over from the Mobile County Public Defender’s Office, the judge had ordered the prosecution to disclose all of its evidence.
“Leading up to the trial, the parties had extensive communication regarding trial, witnesses, and evidence,” Walsh wrote. He added that in the week before the trial in August, he met with prosecutors to review the evidence.
“The Defense believed it possessed all the evidence related to the investigation,” he wrote. It was not until after the trial had begun, Walsh wrote, that he learned the Mobile Police Department had been in possession of the cell phone extraction report for years.
“In fact, its very existence was kept from the Defendant,” he wrote. “As such, the Defense had no reason to file a Motion to Compel. ”
